_what: Corpus-overlap measurement for PMID 30216729 (Sago 2018, Nano Letters). Every query carries a positive control.

_positive_control.expectation: DSPC is a corpus helper lipid and MUST return many rows
_positive_control.why_this_control: if the name-column scan were reading nothing -- a wrong column list, an all-NaN cast -- every token would return 0 and the 7C1 zero would be vacuous

token_pattern_test._interpretation: A substring join on this paper's own tokens is catastrophic and the numbers below quantify it. `7C1` matches nothing by any route, so the ionizable component is genuinely absent -- but `C14` and `C18`, which ARE tokens printed in this paper's formulation tables, match corpus rows in bulk while naming PEG ALKYL TAILS in this paper and something else there. That is the wrong-namespace failure: the token is real, the match is real, and the join is still meaningless.

Cholesterol.why_queried: drawn in full on SI p14

DSPC.why_queried: drawn in full on SI p14

positive_control.why_queried: POSITIVE CONTROL -- not in this paper
positive_control.expectation: DLin-MC3-DMA is documented at ~3,087 corpus rows; a join returning 0 would mean the InChIKey index is broken and every other zero here is uninterpretable

ionizable_component_7C1.why_not: SI p14 draws 7C1 as a GENERIC SCHEME: a C15 epoxide (drawn as R-epoxide with R=C13) reacted with PEI600 in ethanol at 90 C for 72 h. PEI600 is branched, polydisperse polyethylenimine of nominal MW 600, so the product is a distribution over both backbone topology and degree of substitution. No atom-resolved structure is drawn, stated, or derivable, and the paper gives no formula, no HRMS and no NMR for it.
ionizable_component_7C1.precedent: CLAUDE.md section 3: PEG-lipids are deliberately absent from the reagent registry because the block length is a distribution, so no single SMILES is right. 7C1 is the same case on the ionizable component.
ionizable_component_7C1.must_not_be_guessed: Writing a representative monomer would put a made-up structure in IL_SMILES. The brief's rule is to flag, never guess -- and with zero emittable rows there is nothing to flag it on.

substructure_sweep_superset.label: SUPERSET -- a chemotype match is not the same molecule

aminoalcohol_from_epoxide_ring_opening.why: the motif 7C1 would carry: a ring-opened 1,2-epoxide giving N-CH2-CH(OH)-alkyl

aminoalcohol_with_long_tail.why: same motif, tightened to require >=5 further tail carbons

polyamine_backbone_3plus_N.why: a PEI-like ethylenimine run of three nitrogens

tertiary_aliphatic_amine.why: POSITIVE CONTROL -- ionizable lipids are full of these; must be in the thousands or the sweep is reading nothing

sterol_skeleton.why: POSITIVE CONTROL -- cholesterol is the corpus's near-universal sterol; must be non-zero AND must match the registry cholesterol

substructure_sweep_superset.verdict: Even a non-zero chemotype count would not be an overlap: 7C1 has no atom-resolved structure, so it cannot be shown identical to anything. The loose counts are reported as a superset and claimed as nothing more.

invivo_shared_structures.why: 7C1 has no writable structure, so it cannot join this set even in principle, and this paper emits no in-vivo row anyway. It neither adds a third shared in-vivo structure nor raises the source count on either existing one.
